name: Trade war & tariffs
value: Mexico doubling threat 12 Nov; not in force
summary: Trump's 12 Nov threat to double tariffs on Mexico over migrant caravans has not been enacted; no retaliation found
state: President Trump threatened on 12 Nov to double tariffs on Mexico unless it stops migrant caravans heading north (Mexico News Daily; All India Radio, 13 Nov). Searches to 22 Nov found no new tariff increase in force and no retaliation from Mexico, so Watch holds on the threat.
for_you: Firms trading across the US–Mexico border face uncertainty over costs. Consumer prices for affected goods can rise if threatened tariffs take effect.
rubric_hit: Major tariff threatened between large economies = Watch

sources.title: Mexico News Daily — Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico as a new migrant caravan heads north
All India Radio — Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico unless it stops migrant caravans

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
